title: How to Interpret Biblical Prophecy
subtitle: A guide to interpreting Bible prophecy faithfully, understanding what the prophets actually did, how prophecy and fulfillment work, and how to avoid the common abuses that turn the prophets into a crystal ball

sections.title: What We Got Wrong About the Prophets
sections.body:
Say the word prophecy in most churches and people think of prediction. The future, decoded. A roadmap of things to come, hidden in old books, waiting for a clever reader to line them up with the news.

That is a thin and mostly false picture of what the prophets were. Far more of their work was about their own present than about any distant future.

The prophet was a covenant prosecutor. He stood in God's courtroom and indicted a people who had broken faith. He thundered against injustice, idolatry, and the crushing of the poor. He called Israel back to the God who rescued them. Foretelling the future was real but secondary, and even that was almost always tied to the present call to repent. Read the prophets as a crystal ball and you will miss most of what they said. Read them as God's lawsuit against a faithless people, and as his stubborn promise to save them anyway, and you will finally hear them.

sections.title: Forthtelling Before Foretelling
sections.body:
The prophets spent most of their breath telling the truth about now, not predicting then. They named the sin in front of them. They held up the covenant Israel had signed and showed the nation how far it had drifted. They afflicted the comfortable and comforted the afflicted.

This is forthtelling. Speaking God's word into the present moment, with all its fire. The foretelling, when it came, served this.

When Amos cried for justice to roll down like waters, he was not predicting. He was prosecuting. When Hosea married a faithless wife, he was acting out God's anguish over a people that would not stay. The future judgments and the future hope they announced were the logical end of the present choices, the natural fruit of covenant kept or broken. So when you read a prophet, ask first what he was saying to his own people in his own crisis. Get that, and any prediction inside it will sit in its proper place, rooted, not floating free for you to attach to today's headlines.

sections.title: How Fulfillment Actually Works
sections.body:
Prophecy and fulfillment do not work like a vending machine, one coin in, one exact prediction out. The New Testament writers handle prophecy in ways that surprise a flat reader. A word spoken about Israel coming out of Egypt is applied to Christ. A pattern repeats and deepens across centuries.

Prophecy often works in layers. A near fulfillment in the prophet's own time, and a fuller, final fulfillment in Christ that the first only foreshadowed.

Isaiah promised a child whose birth would be a sign to a king in his own day, and the Gospel writer hears in it the deeper note of God with us in Jesus. The return from exile happened, and it pointed past itself to a greater rescue from a deeper bondage. This is not the New Testament playing loose with the text. It is the New Testament reading the prophets the way they were built to be read, as words that aim past their first horizon at the Christ who is the goal of all of them. Watch for the layers, and you will not flatten the prophets into single point predictions they were never meant to be.

sections.title: Christ Is the Key to the Prophets
sections.body:
On the road to Emmaus, the risen Jesus took two heartbroken disciples through Moses and all the Prophets and showed them how the whole thing was about himself. That walk is the master class in reading prophecy. The prophets were not finally pointing at a date on a calendar. They were pointing at him.

Every prophetic hope, for a King, a kingdom, a cleansed temple, a forgiven people, a new heart, a new creation, converges on Christ.

This is the discipline that keeps you from chasing prophecy down endless speculative roads. Ask of any prophetic text how it finds its yes in Jesus. The day of the Lord, the suffering servant, the shepherd God promised to send, the Spirit poured out on all flesh, all of it lands on him in his first coming or waits for him at his return. Read the prophets toward Christ and they cohere. Read them apart from Christ and they fracture into a thousand competing theories, each with its own chart, none with the Lamb at the center.

sections.title: The Abuses to Refuse
sections.body:
The errors here are old and predictable. The newspaper method, which matches verses to current events and revises the matches every time the events move on. The date setting, which the Bible itself forbids, since no one knows the day or the hour. The endless chart making that turns the prophets into a puzzle for insiders.

Every generation has confidently identified the final beast and the imminent end. Every generation so far has been wrong.

I have lived long enough to watch certainty after certainty quietly expire. The names changed, the dates passed, the books went out of print, and the church that hung its faith on them was left embarrassed. The prophets were not given to make you a forecaster of geopolitics. They were given to make you faithful. Refuse the abuses, not because the future is unimportant, but because the abuses steal attention from the present obedience the prophets actually demanded. Watch and be ready, the way a servant watches for a master. That readiness, not a chart, is what prophecy asks of you.

sections.title: Read the Prophets to Be Changed
sections.body:
So interpret prophecy by first listening for the word to its own time. Watch for the layers of fulfillment. Read every prophet toward Christ. And refuse the speculation that has embarrassed the church in every age.

The goal was never to know the future. It was to fear God in the present and trust the Christ the prophets pointed to.

The prophets did not come to satisfy our curiosity about the end of the world. They came to break our hearts over sin and bind them up with hope. They came to make a comfortable people uncomfortable and a despairing people sure. If your study of prophecy leaves you confident about dates but unchanged in your living, you have read the prophets and missed them entirely. Let them prosecute you, then let them comfort you, then let them point you to Christ. That is what they were for. Read them to be changed, not to predict.
